For a game that is a Visual Novel, Written in the Sky is pretty short... And I wouldn't have a problem with it, as Without Within (another free Visual Novel game available on Steam) was even short than this one... But the biggest diference between these two games was that Without Within's story actually made sense. It was short, yet I didn't get the feeling it was rushed. Written in the Sky, however, is a different story. The game starts off with the main character, Azure, an "18 year old" girl who acts and looks more like she's 14, in all honesty. She hates school although she doesn't give a valid reason for it. And she likes to act like a cat. And that's all there is to Azure's personality. She lives with her father, who apparently is invisible... either that or the developers didn't care about him. He's a detective and works until very late... And that's about is all the info we get about him.
One night. Azure sneaks out and gets lost, ends up following Sienna, an alien girl from Mars who's looking for a ring. They both end up in a sort of warehouse and Azure finds the ring. The ring ends up being a Martian wedding ring, or a "hlhlglgkgj" ring in Martian language, and they are bound to each other for life. And that's where the real story ends... That's halfway through the game. The rest of the game involves a +18 love scene, with a minimum amount of nudity... Seriously, the only reason why it can be called a love scene is because of the text that you read throughout it... Even that felt rushed. And there's the ending, that also felt rushed. Also, why the hell was an Optimus Prime-looking-thing at the end?! Couldn't you get a bit more creative, developers? The only difference between the real Optimus Prime and this one is that the one in the game is green, otherwise it would look the EXACT SAME. - sigh - Very creative, devs....
Seriously. the only pros are that the game is free (thankfully, I wouldn't pay for it even if it costed 1 cent), and you can get two easy achievements... Though, if I were you, I wouldn't bother getting them.
I give this one a 4/10, and that's being generous. A good thirty-something minutes wasted for nothing. I could have spent my time with something better.

It’s a survival game, but it’s not what you think. There are no zombies – for once! This War of Mine is just you and some other survivors who are living in an active war zone, trying to stay warm and survive until you can leave the city.
I was able to beat the game on my first time touching the game, which I heard is not a typical experience. The game can prove to be a challenge, and will certainly test your morality. Is it ok to rat out your neighbour in exchange for food? Is it ok to steal from the defenceless? Are all humans really fit for survival?
The art style is also unique, but don’t let the 2D platformer style fool you. The game does function very well for being played on platforms. Even some survivors will be able to navigate better than others will.
Will you put hundreds of hours into the game? No, but you will certainly get your money’s worth.

I played World of Warcraft for awhile, and the game-within-the-game in Cibele had the same "what the heck am I really doing here?" and "I'm paying WoW to waste hours of my time doing this over and over again?"  Like, the monsters get more challenging, you level up, nothing really changes.  At least Cibele, the game, had some depth to it. It was not just running around killing monsters.
The music was atmospheric, and I enjoyed the treatment of the various videos.  I couldn't tell if they had intentionally ran them through different lighting/filters to illicit different moods, or if the person shooting was an amateur, but the game is supposed to have an "amateur" feel to it.  Selfies, meeting for the first time, trying to keep on top of writing your blog, having friends upset with you for ignoring them and drafts of college papers.  None of this is professional.  But I don't think it's supposed to be.
I liked how things swapped back and forth, and there was a good balance between interactive pieces like the game-within-a-game and the desktop, and the non-interactive "cut scene" videos.
Overall, if I could say one thing about this game is that, even with me clicking on and responding to everything in the game - taking my time and exploring, it took me precisely 180 minutes (on the clock) to complete from start to finish. That's a short game.
For what I spent on the game - a little over $10 - I feel like maybe two and a half hours might have been worth it if...
1) The game had achievements.  I'm an acheivement nut.  I prefer games that give them to me, even if I don't have to really do much to earn them. I think there would be a few places where you could earn them, though:
* Just for buying/starting the game
* Clicking 100/500/1000 times in the game-within-a-game
* Making it all the way to the end
* Clicking all the available files on the "computer"
* Reading and/or responding to every incoming message
2) I half expected the game to be longer. Like, maybe twice as long?  I did not feel closure at the end, but, as mentioned earlier, maybe I wasn't supposed to feel any?  Maybe a sequel, or an update to the existing game?  It's art, I know.  It is what it is, and maybe this is the way the game needs to end.  I can just make up an ending in my head anyway. Right?  Can't we all?
3) I wanted to punch the guy at the end.  I'd already clicked a bunch in the game, why not add an arcade element to the end?  A cartoony version of his "ghost dude" face, "click to punch" until you get a KO.  Maybe not politically correct, but still.  Dude deserved it.
4) The game should have had collectible cards because, as in the case of achievements, I love to be able to collect cards, create badges, and add additional XP to my Steam profile.  The cards and badges would be SO easy to make, as the art team on this project has a certain look and feel that would make for a fun indie set of collectibles.
If you don't want to spend $10 on this game, just go join an on-line dating service, and eventually, you will find a person of your preferred gender like the guy in this game, who's into you, but not that into you.  If you're lucky, it won't end up like this game ended.

Concealed in the monstrous Himalayas lies a country ingrained in tradition and brutality. You become Ajay Ghale, returning to the country of his birth, the this forests and formidable snow capped summits of Kyrat, to fulfill your mother’s dying wish of spreading her ashes. This bitter and unpredictable country offers visitors opportunity and danger. You quickly find yourself ensnared in a rebellion to overthrow the thorny regime of Pagan Min, a statesman known as much for his sense of style and charisma as for his cruelty and naked brutality. Navigating the treacherous landscape, you find your fate increasingly linked to the choices you make because in Kyrat, and every second is a story. In Far Cry 4, you’ll conquer fortress outposts from the back of a 6-ton elephant and hit the skies as you rain down explosives from your moving perch in the gyrocopter. The vertical landscape of the Himalayas isn’t just a gorgeous backdrop, but a playground that encourages the player to fight, hunt and explore, grappling cliffs or launching into the air, plummeting to the valley underneath your feet in a controlled free fall with your wing suit. You’ll carry with you a unique arsenal of weaponry that lets you play as you will, whether it’s sniping, sneaking or all-out assault. When all else fails, animals can be your biggest allies or your greatest peril.

If you enjoyed FC3, you'll enjoy Far Cry 4, as it is essentially an overpriced expansion.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Basically a Nepalese expansion for Far Cry 3, the gameplay mechanics and general premise are identical, the only changes being the setting and the higher fidelity graphics. Much like Just Cause, this game isn't driven by plot, but simple, fun gameplay in an open world full of collectibles.
The plot line itself only takes a few hours, if that (it took me 35 hours, but that includes finishing all of the side missions on top of the plot missions, and doing a fair amount of the collectibles. Maybe another 5-10 hours to get them all). Infact, the plot is probably the worst part of the game. A stunning graphical project for £4, A tech demo really but a detailed and enjoyable experiance.
To start off i dont normally make reviews but i felt i needed to in with this demo so please bare with my on this one.
The Lost Valley in all of its amazing detail graphically is at heart only a playable tech demo, When we enter the Demo for the first time we are presented with a great setting of an idyllic forest where everything seems to be in harmony.
For the first couple of minuets of this game you are put into a sence of calm and you are left to take in the surroundings and the atmospheric scene that is left before you. This however does not last very long.
The first thing that hits you when you start to take your walk is the lack of ambiant sound effects, While yes there are some in the game they seem to only be triggered at certain points, The walking should be a constant sound effect, But i only heard it a couple of times throughout the whole demo. There was no wind brushing though the trees, There was no wildlife or sounds of water when walking through the ponds. All these things while easy to place into the game should i fell have been there thoughout rather than just at triggered moments in the demo.
The next thing to mention is the soundtrack used in the demo, It is awful the first couple of minuets the sound track is the one used in the trailer which in my opinion i was all for i love that type of harmonic music, It all went down hill when that track had finished, It was then replaced by what i can only describe as somone mashing random keys on a piano it was grating and the game lost all of its idyllic setting, I found myself wanting to get to the end alot quicker.
Graphically i cannot fault the demo ,Cryengine is one of if not the best engine on the market at the moment, With it's easy to use machanics and high levle of quality cryengine was an ideal choice for this type of demo. Some things for the devs though, I have worked with cryengine in the past and i noticed the in-game CC was not locked, I was messing around with some commands and while most of the settings where ideal for the experiance there where things like, Level of Detail, Particles, Image Post-Processing and Fps Cap i found myself changing to give a better visual experiance.
As far as the actually game play is concerned the is not much to it you walk crouch and jump, While crouching and jumping are in the Demo there is no real need for them to be used as the whole Demo can be finished without them, While walking around there is only one point i found myself walking off the track to a building, one thing that would of been a nice thing to add is the ability for explore even if it was to the point of entering buildings or multiple paths to give the Demo some reply value.
All in all i did enjoy the experiance, If they would remove the piano soundtrack and add the things i mentioned in the review it would complete this game. For £4 i would reccommend this while short in lenght it is a well designed concept of what Cryengine can do.

This game is lovely.
Build your own metro lines!
Simply drag from one station to another to draw your line. The three basic stations are circle (common), triangle (uncommon) and square (rare), passengers will want to travel from their current station to a station that matches their shape, e.g. a triangle passenger currently at a circle station will want to go to a triangle station. Over time new unique station variants appear to complicate the map and other extras are introduced slowly.
Pros:
+ Intuative gameplay
+ Very nice minimalistic art, simplistic interface and controls
+ Relaxing background music and sound effects gel well with theme
+ Idividual games are not too long, generally 30 minutes (+/- 10 minutes)
+ Each map is different, with different rules and regulations, such as the maximum number of trains per line or number of seats per carriage - this is not explicitly stated in game (that I have seen) but these are nice to stumble across
+ Very relaxing, a great game for stress reduction
+ Features an even less stressful endless mode
+ Very addictive
Cons:
- Removing stations from the middle of a line can be a bit fiddly but you will eventually get the hang of it (drag the line inbetween the station you want to remove and the next station over the station you want to remove)
- The random station spawns can get frustrating when you have 5 circles in a row!
Would very much recommend to anyone, especially for someone looking for a relaxing puzzle game or a building game

Minimalist graphics.
Train logistics.
Slow building where each scenario starts with 3 stations, then adds new stations and passengers over time.
By far, what I find most satisfying about this game, is watching the train simulation, watching passengers get on and off trains.  The mechanism is the same as other train simulators and the lightweight graphics don't detract from the experience and immersion.
The logistics consist of creating paths so common passenger destinations are accessible in minimal stops, while rare destinations are still handled in a timely fashion.  Also, just because a station is full and a train arrives, doesn't mean anybody will get on board, since the passengers seem to choose a train going to the nearest destination, not the earliest destination... (i.e. they'll wait a week to get on the train which has their stop next, rather than getting on this train that has their stop 2 stops down in the other direction) - at least it looked like that's what they are doing.
Choose between new engine types, new routes, bridges, or carriages.  As stations become overcrowded with unserviced passengers, eventually the scenario will end, with an option to continue in endless mode.  Endless mode is fun as the game turns into mostly a free-form sandbox train station simulator.  Setting up one train to have a long chain of cars is pretty nice.
I loved Sid Meier's Railroad and Mini Metro provides a lot of the same enjoyment.  Gameplay starts a little too slow, and after about 2 minutes picks up enough to become interesting.  Good tension.  Each map seems to generate stops randomly, so the same map played twice can be very different.  It would be nice to have an RNG seed interface to play the same map and station order repeatedly, but the game is still enjoyable as it is.  $10 - fair price.

Sometimes going in blind works out and sometimes you wish you had a time machine to go back and make up for all those hours you wasted. I randomly chose Avencast: Rise of the Mage from my ever growing Steam library knowing absolutely nothing about the game. This can be fun because without any expectations the experience can be natural. Unfortunately it didn’t pay off.
Avencast is a high fantasy RPG that seems to be trying to shoot for the fences but just doesn’t hit the mark for me personally. Right away you’re thrown into this standard run of the mill story. You play as a child found by the side of the river discovered by an old man who raises you as his own. As you grow older your interest in magic grows as well so the old man sends you to a school for mages called Avencast. This is where the game begins. It just seems standard as hell to me and the characters themselves aren’t all that interesting. I found it just boring actually. With these specific kinds of games story telling and creating a wonderful world filled with interesting characters is key to making a epic RPG that the player wants to spend hundreds of hours in. It doesn’t deliver. Then there is the gameplay situation.
The game has a top down/isometric camera position and allows you to zoom in and out but for the life of me I couldn’t find a position that felt good. I was either to close behind my character or to far away to see my surroundings. Movement was awkward as well. In battle mode your movement feels decent but when running in exploration mode it just felt sluggish to me. The voice acting sounds like I’m being read a bedtime time story. Not natural and almost robotic at times. All these things just turned me off.
It’s not all bad! Combat was actually pretty fun. The player has close quarters and range attacks that can be switched on the fly and feels very satisfying. You also unlock skills that make you feel like a bad♥♥♥♥♥wizard. The loot system is good too. You will constantly find better equipment to aid you on your quest. Still these positives don’t outweigh the negatives and I just can’t recommend this to a friend.
My opinions are my own. If you love this game that’s all that matters so more power to you. I also realize that people devoted huge chunks of their lives to work on this game and I respect them for that. I have no idea how hard it is to develop or work on a game. I’m just another player with an opinion. Thank you.

The game has captured my heart in the 2 hours that I have played it, but I'm gonna look at it objectively for a review standpoint.
PROS:
- Beautiful art
- Awesome and pretty unique character design
- Interesting game mode which is based around your two living guardians instead of capture points or towers and such as in DOTA or LoL or Overwatch (all of which i enjoy equally)
- Good business model (you can purchase cosmetics with ingame currency as well as real money)
- Smooth gameplay
- Interesting Fortune Card (quest) mechanic
CONS:
- Only 19 heroes on launch, which is basically the only problem that I have with the game.
- I have heard people saying that the game is not balanced, but I believe that with the roster of heroes at your disposal, it is quite balanced, it's just that people don't know it yet since it's relatively new (fresh launch)

Kinda fun game, but suffers from a clusterf*** interface.
So here's how the game works.  You start out on a somewhat massive floor that's been randomly generated and filled with monsters.  Every time you click or move a square, you'll use a turn.  The gameplay somewhat resembles Diablo 2, but the developer went nuts and made the whole interface a mess.  You custom generate a character with something like 6 skills you choose.  Every time you advance a level, you can improve one of these skills.
Here's where things turn into a mess.  The character sheet has something like 30-50 stats that you can increase.  You have no idea what 90% of them do, but every item or skill will improve or lower several of them.  The major difference between this and Diablo 2 is that Diablo 2 stopped at 4 resistances and 5-6 stats.  Dungeons of Dredmore has 50 and it bundles them altogether in one cramped section that gives you a headache just looking at it.
Because of what I mentioned above, the skill system is completely meaningless. I have no idea what would be a good thing to level up. Unless I spend an hour deciphering the stat screen, which I don't plan to do.
Same problem with items.  I just find the most expensive item and equip it...  I have no idea what is "good" in this game.
Another problem is the flavorless monotony that is the gameplay.  You are dropped into the middle of a floor full of monsters and have to clear it.  Then you go onto the next floor and do the same thing.  Then the next and the next.  In Diablo 2 they had some storyline to break up the monster killing.  Stories about this horrible monster and that horrible monster.  However, Dungeons of Dredmor has NONE of that.  Just one floor of monsters after the next.
On a technical note, when you start the game for the first time, the game will let you set whatever resolution you like including ones WAY OVER your monitor's capibility.  If you do this, the buttons at the top of the screen won't be visible and you'll be stuck at the main menu until you fix the resolution.

Aside from the flaws, it really is a fun game and after spending 130+ hours playing it I will go back for more every now and then.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

I enjoyed this game. It has quality graphics, AI is reasonable, and you have some variation in that you can play as pure Ghost, going silent, unseen, and without even knocking someone out. Or, you can prey on the Watch with Sawtooth arrowheads from afar, spring environment traps, or best them in CQC. Biggest drawback for me is that while there is definitely a much larger 'World' in general, the campaign does limit the openness of it, and it sometimes begins to feel rather linear.
Some of the complaints I've seen are kind of preposterous; "Too much loot" but at the same time "Why can't I sell Unique loot items?" What do you need to sell the coolest items for when you are already supposedly swimming in loot? I admit I don't spend time reviewing my stash of Collectible items, but I appreciate the hunt to complete those collections!
Also, people knocking the plot, and/or voice acting? I don't know what they thought was so great about the storyline of the first Thief games, but I must have overlooked it somehow. The plot, however fantastical, makes as much sense as one can in an alternate reality. If you buy games for the voice acting, maybe you should just stick to watching movies.
Some have also noted the button-tapping in certain transitional areas, while not great, I'd rather have this than a loading screen every time I move to different segment of the City.
I like the bit of motion-blur, head-bob, and leaning into corners while you are running as well- makes me feel like im actually moving through the environment rather than just passing over it.
If you are a HARDCORE fan who expects this to be TDP but with modern graphics, and feature-film quality voice acting, stay home, or wait for a deep discount. Otherwise I can recommend this game for those interested in the stealth genre.

You're literally reading a book, and deciding on a few conversation choices that is seemingly pointless. Storyline is great, but I do feel that it is a little draggy and slow. Nonetheless, when it starts to perk up to the mysteries, it kicks in well. The art style in this VN strikes the word odd to me. In the spaceship, all the backgrounds pops out at you with a feeling of being detailed. Yet when you leave the ship to an outdoor scene, the backgrounds are less detailed, seemingly a quick painting sketch(it still looks detailed, but how should I put it... unlined or dabbling paint blobs?) Even within the spaceship, some backgrounds look a bit more on the realistic side, and some other scenes more cartoonish. At the end of the day, it's alright I guess.
So. Remember i started off with saying that this is a visual novel more than a game? Well at the end of the day, some people may find this VN engaging for the storyline, while some may deter from this for the lack of gameplay. My initial reaction (10 hours) is: Great!! .
Pros and cons this far:
+ Customization:
weapon tuning:
Quite extensive! Barrel, muzzle, grips, optics, flaslights, laser sights... etc etc, even for pistols. (I laughed placing a gigantic sniper scope and huge silencer on a pistol).
Game modes:
Classic mode (no "super powers"), allow or dissalow weapon types etc. Whatever you like to play, it's there.
Characters:

+ Firing range, AI bots (try any weapon in game, practise aiming)
+ Large playerbase

Avencast is an Action RPG that looks old and feels old. It's like the devs did not have any creativity at all and simlpy thought to make some easy cash by salvaging tons of common things about phantasy and just see where it gets them. At least you, as a buyer can be certain about what you are getting here - typical phantasy ARPG with linear story and an easy combat system.
Now on to details:
The story is absolutely linear and obvious since the first intro video. You were born being special and everyone in the main quest line keeps reminding you that the whole world is placed on your shoulders pretty much in every single quest after the tutorial. Whats even worse is that the whole story has been used billion times in other games - betrayal, invasion by demons, big bad guy threatening to destroy everything and you are the only one to stop him. The side quests are nothing but fatch quests having no connection to the main quest at all. During the whole game you will see about 10 differant map layouts and about 10 different type of enemies. Everything else is just being salvaged and re-used. In the whole game I've seen only a single enemy that was not reminding me of exactly the same in other games.
At the start I thought that the combat fun gonna pick itself up when I get more spells and attacks. Sadly, it doesnt. Instead of spamming basic attacks, after skilling higher level spells I started spamming them. The choice is also not huge since you need one single target attack and one AoE to progress through the whole game. Besides that higher level skills in Avencast are mostly just upgraded versions of lower level ones.The only choice that matters is the skill type - melee or ranged, since the influenced by different stats. The AI is simply garbage, even worse than stupid, since it gets stuck a lot of times just trying to reach you. Same for NPCs that follow you in some quests. In battle the monsters simply run at you in a straight line, from time to time dodging to the side but thats kinda it. Even the monsters with shields either un at you or stand still "blocking" for 3 seconds and continue running at you again. Avencast offers no challange even at hardest difficulty whatsoever.There are tons of RPGs, especially action RPGs that have innovative or remarkable fighting systems and sadly Avencast doesnt use any ideas from these, neither inventing anything new or creative.
The graphic feels quite aged, its not insanely bad but definetely not up to 2010 release date. A lot of areas dont feel detailed enough, there is no eye candy to get any attention. The characters take some time getting used to, since its a mix of older RPGs and cartoonish graphic style. Some areas have decent immersion with destroyed objects, but besides that sadly nothing worth mentioning. The interface is absolutely simplistic - few slots for items like potions, few slots for spells. A small ribbon bar for icons like character screen and inventory.
The progress in Avencast is pretty simple - just follow the main quest markers. Sometimes there is a small detour into the room next to the main room on the map to grab a key item, but besides that its always straight forward. It earns few points here though for having some mini-games that either require some reading, thinking or try & error. Some timing and dodging minis at the end of the game also make the game last a bit longer than simply rushing to kill the endboss asap.
I dont even remember, if the game had any music, thats how unremarkable it was. The battle sounds are sounding mostly clunky, no real feedback giving about the impact of the hits. Playing as a ranged character the whole game I was listening to 2 different attack sounds for 12 hours. Since there are barely any differencies between the monsters, their sounds are being reused aswell. The only good immersion with sound feedback was inside the starting room where you could hear background chatting of the crowd with distinguishable words. After that the devs probably decided its not worth the time spending on immersion and sound feedback.
I hope this review helps you making the decision if its worth buying this game. Rate and leave a comment if you enjoyed reading it.

Game itself is pretty good, but not without issues..
Nice graphics, but not without issues and it has unity written all over it, with horrendous fps sinks/hanging, but it's a game that will look good even years after launch, thanks to art style.
Soundtrack is nice and catchy, no complains there.
Plot is engaging and pretty good. Even though characters are stereotypes of voodoo/goth chick, stupid grunt, smart guy etc., it fits. While at first there might be a lot of questions and it can get somewhat confusing, it is all answered at the end of the game.
Problem with this game is how short on content it is and lacking puzzle aspect. Game holds your hand for the most time, so there is not much thinking required. You have time constrains, but there are no consequences or anything. It's worse, because game is downright lying by saying something like "changing one thing might end up being worse" - I didn't notice a chance to do that, since the game is linear and only opens the whole mansion near the end and you have clear objective you must do. Ending is both good and awful - good, because it gives nice conclusion, but bad from the game perspective, because the game turns into visual novel. As far as I know, there is no auto option for the dialog, so you have to press right mouse button every time speech bubble appears. And there is quite a few of them. What also sucks is the whole confession thing, because you were there, you've seen that, so there is no need to pad out the game even more.
The game isn't challenging at all - ever played Neighbours from Hell? It's pretty much the same game deal, only darker. You watch what is happening, and then do whatever you have to do to advance. Some soultions feel somewhat random, and one moment, I swear, got inspired by Discworld adventure game, where you had to throw the log into the fireplace to make it further.
I guess the only replay value here might be unlocking alternate ending by collecting whole deck of cards, but it is thankfuly not time consuming, because most of cards you will get by playing.
It is fine game to play, just not for full price or even sale price, because it is short and lacks replay value (unless you don't care about that and just want to play the game - then just get it and enjoy it). Once you beat it, you will probably not come back to it, maybe years later, although that's rare with adventure games like this. It is perfect bundle game and if you will have another chance to get it (it was bundled twice already) then get it and play it, because it is good.

Well, this is something different.
This is a simple game, whose sole aim is to facilitate the feeling and atmosphere of socialization through MMORPGs, including multiple parallel private chats and even more multitasking with the mail client and an Instagram app, all while playing the game. And it does this pretty well. It made me remember my life back when I used to play WoW a lot.
This game is an idea - an instense idea charged with emotion. It feels very raw and extremely personal. Being allowed to go through her desktop, reading chat logs and looking and sent pictures, felt very intimate. It really plays with one's voyeuristic curiosity. Then there are the voice chats, which again feel like overhearing someone's intimate conversation - full of sighs and "hmmm". Nine is a charming and pleasant-sounding person, whose voice I found enjoyable. But the central events quickly unfold and end. One hour, and you're done (including browsing through the contents of the computer).
Before playing this game, I read an interview with the creator (Nina) about it. Concerning the central plot, I feel I got almost as much from this reading as I did from the actual game. The main difference was in the details. The game is just much better at conveying emotions and re-creating the atmosphere.
Overall, while I can't say that I didn't enjoy this game, I was left with a strong desire that it was deeper, that there was more to it. In its current form it felt like a mere illustration of an idea, rather than a full-scale experience I came to expect from games.
In its essence, this is a intriguing, but tiny art project. I feel that those that would appreciate the game already see parallels with their own life and want to experience a short, but intense surge of nostagia and tickle their voyeuristic curiosity.

I really wanted to like this game. I like quirky, unusual games. I like alternative or unusual storytelling methods. I want female developers to succeed because their gender should make no difference whether or not their games are taken seriously. I like games that explore small, everyday things like a budding online relationship. On paper, this game looked pretty interesting.
Cibele, however, is barely even a game. Pretty much everything about it is just... poor.
I'd love to discuss the game's mechanics, but unfortunately... there are none. As the game unfolds, it alternates between three formats, over three time periods during which the 'relationship' between the girl and boy unfolds:
- a (very user unfriendly) virtual desktop, where you can browse the files, folders, emails etc. of the game's 'protagonist'. I hesitate to use that word, but I'll get onto that in a moment
- the multiplayer game that the 'protagonist' plays. If this were a Flash game hosted on Newgrounds in 1997, it would still be considered terrible by those standards. It's obviously just supposed to act as a placeholder, a window through which we see the interaction between the 'protagonist' and the guy she likes unfold. But it's one-dimensional, horribly made, ugly as sin, and just annoying to 'play'. It's basically a casual clicker game, but worse
- videos of a girl sitting at a computer in her underwear, taking photos of herself in her underwear, and doing other assorted things in her underwear. These make up a tiny portion of the tiny amount of gameplay in this 'game', but make up the vast majority of the screenshots and marketing. Doesn't take a genius to work out why (hint: underwear)
As for the story... I understand that I might not be the target demographic here (male, older than a teenager), but I found it awful to the point of grating. The girl through whom you view the events of the game is a completely one-dimensional, weak character. The's the 'protagonist' of the game only because you play 'through her eyes' - there is never a point in the game where you can make a decision that changes anything. It's entirely linear and on rails - the only reason this simulation can call itself a 'game' is because of the sequences where you play the fake game, and as above, that is awful and basically just completely pointless clicking until the game decides to move you on.
As for the guy that the 'protagonist' falls for... he's a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. He's creepy, he's overbearing, he's pushy, and completely awful. I honestly thought the game was shaping up to be a cautionary tale to tell naive girls not to talk to creeps online.
I thought there might be some intrigue to the way the story unfolds passively - you don't see every interaction between the girl and the boy, you only view their relationship via the three sequences above. For example, the second time you're looking at the girl's desktop, there are new files in her folders, showing a little of what she's done in the meantime. A better storyteller probably could have woven an interesting tale by letting the 'player' fill in missing details, but unfortunately that's not the case here either. The whole thing feels forced and completely artificial.
I understand that probably a fair bit of work went into making this game, so I didn't want to dismiss it with a one word review. But quite honestly, there's probably more content in this review than there is in the game. I'm gonna leave it here.
Want to play a game that tells a story in a unique, alternative way? Try
, or
, or literally anything else. Just don't buy Cibele, it's a waste of money.
Avoid. Avoid it hard.

I recommend this game, but I will freely admit that it will be very hit and miss depending on what kind of games and stories people like. Here's some basic points to touch on (I'm going to skip rating the story itself to prevent spoilers in such a small game; suffice to say that I liked it)
Gameplay:
Nonexistent. This is the epitome of a visual novel, click to advance text and watch the story unfold and occasionally you will be given a choice of actions to take. Some choices only let you hear varying lines of new dialogue, and others will affect which of the endings you will end up seeing. If you aren't a fan of visual novels, this one isn't inventive enough to change your mind and it will likely be the first thing someone can use as an excuse to avoid this game.
Characters:
I find the characters varied and they can be fun to interact with. Al and Sol are rather bland, but the hyperactive security officer Zuri and timid engineer Kylie can have some good moments. My only real complaints are that 1) the game isn't really long enough to flesh out any characters other than Kika and/or Zuri and 2) there aren't really enough opportunities presented that let the characters act as meaningful foils to play off of each other.
My own personal bias towards the game will certainly be placed in this category. I personally resonated with Natalie's story and personality; not just her "Why does everyone else get the fun jobs when I'm so much better suited than them?" attitude. No, I mean the entire thing, mistakes an harsh self-realizations included.
Linguistics:
Okay, time to be brutally honest. While this feels like a natively English script rather than a translation like most visual novels are, there are a few typos (particularly later in the story) that can really be a distraction. I've dealt with far worse scripts in my time playing these kinds of games, but there were a few sentences that had me scratching my head trying to figure out what they meant before I realized it was simply a script error. At time's like these, it feels less like the native script I mentioned and more like a good fan-sub that unfortunately didn't have enough time to proofread their later files before hitting deadline of some sort. This doesn't make the game unplayable by any means, but given that I've seen people condemn perfectly good games for far less, I felt I needed to come clean and mention it.
Art:
The visual presentation of the characters feels distinctly different from the raw anime/manga-inspired designs I've gotten used to, but I can't say that this style is bad. The characters all look pretty nice, and the backgrounds are pleasing to the eye...I still can't understand why anyone would curl their hair into drill shapes though. That will forever be an artistic mystery lost upon my uncultured upbringing I guess.
Music:
Appropriate for the settings. No individually memorable pieces, but I always felt it was enhancing the mood, not hindering it.
Price:
The game's free. Look, if you are on the edge about this game to read reviews about it, then get it. It will cost you no money, and it's not some huge, meandering AAA game that takes an ungodly amount of time to finally get into the main plot. I went on a 100% run without a walkthrough or any outside resources and completed everything in (*looks at logged playtime*) six hours. It's not a huge RPG or anything, so by the time you've gone through the first half hour or so, you will likely have met the characters you will be spending the game with and heard the basic premise of the plot, and for a visual novel, characters and story are pretty much everything. So if the game hasn't grabbed you well enough by that time, then drop it, but the least you could do is give it a shot.

The order of stations, what type they are and what week rewards you get to choose from seem to be somewhat random. It's more about putting out fires and restructuring your metro system before things get out of hand, than it is about anticipating growth and managing the lines proactively.

All this being said, definitely grab this game when it's cheap.

This is a really good game.  It's a lot like HotS combined with Smite, but better than both of those.  The HotS part is that the maps have points you want to control and there's objectives other than just killing enemies.  The Smite part is that you aim manually and it's a 3rd person action game.  Everything is a skill shot, you aim all your abilities and it's highly skill-based.  There are no creeps, just a handful of creatures that stand guard at certain points on the map.  It's not twitchy unless you choose a character who specializes in that, there's probably a class for everyone if you've played a modern video game in the past eight or nine years.

I'm in love with this game.
I was always mildly interested in the game but I ended up receiving it in a Humble Bundle.
I got around to playing it and I can say it was the best 8 hour session I've ever had.
Began at 5 pm one night and suddenly it was 3 am.
Amazing Music- The only game that I've actively bought an OST for. The music gives the game a charm unlike no other and never grew dull throughout my experience. Whether it was the lively jazz or the chillingly haunting singer the music never failed to enchant me.
Additionally the visuals are astonishing. They run well on virtually any graphic setup, and the graphics are beautiful. THe character design is unique and there is heavy visual flavor for all of the characters. The game is striking visually in the setting alone through the variety of locations and perfect detail.
Specifically the story and puzzles involved are very worth it. This is a mystery game at the heart, but it doesn't take itself too seriously. By making the puzzles not insanely difficult it removes the aspects of hints and hand holding and lets the user discover everything by themselves. Even now, there are still pockets of the game I have yet to discover.
There is much to be found in each character's story, but the story of the Sexy Brutale itself is wonderful.
Highly recommend playing the game all the way through, no spoilers, but the ending is definitely worth it.
All in all, it was a powerful and enabling experience that was euphoria for the eyes. 20 seems like a steep cost for what is relatively a short game, but the content is as grounding as a fantastic book, and about the same price. Amazing job by Cavalier Game Studios, and I'll be watching their work for any other gemstones

The lack of straightforward fast travel can make the game a slog near the end, but it is not so bad that you cannot go for 100% on this game(my first full achievement game). I have no idea why but at first glance I thought The Sexy Brutale was a cludo-like multiplayer game. In truth I wasn’t paying much attention to the trailer, nor did I read the official Steam description or the popular tags the first time I was on the store page.
The Sexy Brutale is a very intriguing murder-mystery puzzle game, centred around a mechanic that allows you to bend time in order to save the guests of The Sexy Brutale Casino Mansion from being killed by the mysterious, superbly sarcastic staff. Instead of finding out who killed (or attempts to kill) the guests you witness their deaths first hand and attempt to save them by interacting with the environment and picking up key items. Although you’ll wonder why they’re killing off the guests and who is ordering them to…
This is an interesting concept with each of the 10 guests’ deaths being unique and eventful in their own way. When I had to solve each death I spent way too long on some. Most of the time I’d forget about interacting with certain items like a fish tank, instrumental in solving one of the murders. Some people will breeze through this game, others will take longer which isn’t necessarily a bad thing as the visuals and the music is easily the best part of The Sexy Brutale and have been crafted with a genuine love and care.
If you enjoy puzzle games there is a lot to love here, but whilst some love it I can appreciate this game not being for everyone. I previously said “Some people will breeze though this game”. It could feel rather short to some players which wouldn’t be a problem if it weren’t for the story. It’s odd addressing one of the best/worst things about the entire game. I’m still on the fence about out. I like aspects about it and it has a HUGE twist towards the end which I found intriguing but  I’ll let you decide if you like it (if you don’t buy/finish the game you could always watch a walkthrough, I’ll link one at the bottom just in case). However I can understand if the story leaves something desired for some.
Thank the lord there is a secret ending which is achieved after finishing one of the worst card games ever invented, 52 pickup.
This game has a lot of charm, wit, humour and soul. From watching videos of the creators talking about it, it’s clear they hit the nail right on the head when it came to setting out what they wanted to achieve with this game.
I believe a majority of people would enjoy this game, a minority of people would appreciate the artistic elements of this game and I for one will remember this game as one of the best experiences I’ve ever had with a video game although not everyone’s palette is the same.
Also whoever composed the main theme, have my children.

Avencast is a nice action RPG, with a solid (although somewhat predictable) storyline.
The combat interface took some degree of getting used to, using key combinations to invoke various spells, but by the time I reached the end of the game, I was able to navigate the combat system as if it were choreographing a dance as much as battling hordes of daemons. Additionally, up to 8 spells can be assigned to hotkeys, so if there are spells that are difficult to get the combo right, or ones that are used repeatedly, a hotkey helps tremendously.
The character development is fairly straightforward, with the biggest gotcha if you fail to notice that the same pool of points is used for both learning new spells and increasing character attributes.
Quests are generally fairly straightforward, and clearly explain well what one needs to do, with a marker on the minimap to remind one of which way to go for quest goals.
There are some puzzles, which can all be solved easily enough if one explores and reads everything.
The graphics are pretty good, for the time that the game came out.
The ambient music and sound effects establish a mood that fits the environments well.
The scripts were reasonably good, and the voice acting was okay, but for several NPC interactions, it sounds like they're speaking in an echo chamber.
Other than that, all I can say is that it was a fun game that had a coherent story, a novel combat system, and fairly well-balanced combat encounters, with reasonable puzzles.

Awesome tycoon-style gameplay. Incredible message, mood, and general point. The issue is, the message and the gameplay clash strongly, since the latter is very fun.
Even though the game is tough and your party will most likely get destroyed, the scavenging and survival themselves rarely leave you frustrated or depressed; there is always the feeling that if things go south, you can attempt something new. Characters sad? Stop looting and try honest barter. Not enough materials? Go on a killing spree. It doesn't necessarily mean you'll succeed; I'm talkig about the
of never being in a truly desperate situation.
Which is truly an awesome feat of game design... but isn't it supposed to be the opposite?
I guess the thing is, This War of Mine expects you to play with your own head, making the conscience of the player a mechanic on its own. When characters complain and suffer, you're supposed to feel bad, even if there are no straightforward penalties.
Do you? That probably depends on the player. I'd say on consecutive walkthroughs the chances are slimmer, while the unrestricted fun of gathering resources never goes away.
Still, it's great that this game exists.

The gameplay in this MMO is terrible.
It's buggy, it's laggy (my machine is more than capable of a lagfree experience so I don't know where that came from), and it's uninspired. One could argue that it isn't too important if the gameplay is solid when the story is so lovingly told. I would argue that means the gameplay has to be even better. Tell me an inovative story (which they did for games), but also give some innovative gameplay.
Simple things like polishing it up, making sure it runs properly would have done enough that I wouldn't be distracted by it (which sadly it took me out of the story). Maybe have Nina's character logout of the game after a fight with Blake? (something like in Depression Quest when agency was purposefully taken away from the player can be pretty impactful) That would require a slight restructuring of the story but still.
Aside from the fake MMO () gameplay it was good. I hope the developers use it as a learning experience and make something where all the aspects are as good as the story.

Here is a strange thing about attraction: Sometimes, you only like a person enough to sleep with them exactly once.
The strange and sad thing is that sometimes you have no idea who these people will be until you actually do it.

And only you can decide how you want to carry that: How much you believe them, how much you care yourself, how much you want to think of it as a part of growing up, or how much you can accept that looking back on ♥♥♥♥♥♥ things with a certain amount of fondness is weird and strange and true.

This isn't a game. Lemme get that out there right away. The gameplay is merely a means to hold you up so that the voiceovers can do their work. That said, it simulates mmo grinding extremely well.
This is the short story of one person's experience in an online relationship, molding together themes from both first loves to young loves. It doesn't matter that it happens to take place online; these feelings are generally universal amongst most human beings, perhaps being unknown to the absolute fringe most antisocial.
This work seems specifically to be an interesting act of coping with what was obviously a rough period in her life. Or, as many people have experienced, an amazing period that ended in such a way that it made all that time completely horrible.
Is this specific work relatable to everyone, though? No. Not everyone went through the same internet-specific relationships the author did. Many more have nowadays, and even more will in the near future, but someone looking for a video game won't find such a thing here. Those who did have such a relationship probably heard every line spoken or written in this game in their own life off-script, with just the names changed. Most of these lines are even universal to facetoface relationships.
Poor things: the cinematography is somewhat lackluster. It's not bad for an amateur work, but each scene didn't seem to speak video-wise the same way the emotions were coming out audio-wise. I don't really review movies, though, so I guess I can't give good criticisms here.
Blake's voice actor wasn't nearly as good as Nina's (Nina herself? I didn't check lmao) as delivering awkwardness. His lines felt just a bit forced when he is supposed to be a charismatic guild leader. Personal chats are always different, but the way he is presented and the way he acts seem to not synergize.
And, of course, the gameplay being nonexistent.
Overall, I related to this work, and therefore it was worth playing. Was it worth the gate cost? Probably not, but that doesn't bother me much.

Interesting autobiographical vignette into someones life at specific moments in time, filtered through their computer desktop, online game world and avatar.   Cibele invites you to explore the perspective of the naive central protagonist (Nina) and her burgeoning online romance; with all the embarresment, awkwardness and uncertainty you might expect, cocurrent with typical (maybe satirical) MMO grinding.
There is very little player agency given you are emphatically put in someone elses position.  You get to know the proganist by having unfettered access to her computer files including photos, old poems, blog posts and chat posts.  The result is uncomfortably voyueristic, and the effective use of cut-scenes to deliniate between the 'real' and the 'virtual' adds to this.
The relationship between the real and the virtual worlds is a major theme as the 'virtual' is interrogated both as a space that facilitates genuine openness, sharing and connection, but also carefully cultivated representations and fantasy/projection.   The relationship itself and the love interest are open to interpretation from our limited perspective; we can chart how events unfold and transcribe what was said, but never really know their thought processes or intentions.  Just what they choose to show us.
...And isn't that always the way?

is minimalist puzzle game themed around mass transportation. The goal is to pick up and deliver passengers by connecting stations to your system with a limited number of resources based on trains and lines. With a design that is both sleek and intuitive, the game requires little in terms of explanation for a new player. It's so easy to pick up that it comes as a shock when the game suddenly crushes your pathetic metro system under the weight of cruel reality.
The negative points about randomized station generation and lack of thematic depth should be taken with the caveat that these were obviously purposeful choices, made to elevate the minimalist design. I personally found the game very enjoyable and would recommend it to anyone looking for an interesting take on transportation games.

Indeed, this game could've been better...
but does it worth a negative review? I don't think so...
Let's start with what's good about this game...
- Despite what lots of voices said since its relase, the game is not a remake or a "game on its own" like the Mad Max one.
Its a sequel of the old Thief Saga, so, both new and old Garrett existed in this universe... lots of clues and little "easter eggs" about this are present in the game (including an entire level in a "familiar place" and a special loot who will make the old fans squirm when they'll find it.)
-IT'S NOT A DISHONORED BOOTLEG
- The City is huge, and full of secrets, passages, you can do a little of parkour on the roofs (but a very limited thing, don't expect Mirror's Edge or Assassin's Creed) the only problem is that, like in the old games, the map is difficult to understand, but i guess is a developer choice..
- The game design is wonderful, when you're in the City, you're IN the City, streets are well made,you're really immersed in this chaos of streets and buildings, in those little slums, or in the big streets, you can even smell the streets, you can fell the cold night around you...
- (I know it's a minor thing, but, let's be honest, it's a first person game, so you'll see them pratically for all the gameplay), Garret's hand are maybe one of the best thing in the game... well modelled and also quite expressive
- The game leave to you the possibility to add to the Hub the radar of the level, the Life Bar etc... but you can turn them off. Even the "Concentration" can be turned off in the options if you think it's too much easy with it. Also, the difficulty of the game, unlike the previous installment, it's perpetual, you choose it in the beginning of the game and stop.
- To me, the introduction of a "level of alert on the enemies is a good thing, I don't know if it can be turned off.
Now, the bad stuff...
- Despite being kinda fluid, the game use to heavily drop the framerate when you enter in a new area, especially if there is something going on there... the framerate eventually come back to fluid after some seconds, so there's nothing to worry about...
- I think the awfullest thing in the game is the audio... especially on the enemies and Bots... it's glichy... and way too much repetitive... I know that for today's standards if you don't run like an idiot for 3/4 of the game you're a noob... but, starting from the fact that Garrett is "a Ghost" (as he sentenced) you SHOULD walking a little slow, especially near enemies, so, if they'll frequentelly starting to repeat the same dialogue over and over, You'll eventually going mad after a while...
- Sometimes, level design is a little unfair, often you cannot find some places to climb, buttons to switch or collectibles o pick up...
- the plot is a little inconsistent... the characters are quite enjoyable in the design... and that's all.
-Despite being not the same Garrett, this new Garrett truly is trying hard to be Cynical like his predecessor so i give a point for trying...
- Cheap jumpscares are cheap, but you'll not see some of them coming...
-bugs are presents here and there... but nothing that can break the game
-It's Unreal engine, so expect some textures not being loaded correctly...
-there's a little enviroment puzzle in the City streets, but the way you'll get the reward will not let you satisfyed...
- Artificial Intelligence should be renamed: artificial deficency.
So... What can I say? If you're not a fan of the Thief Franchise... I don't think it's the game to start with... but if you know the Thief saga, please, don't be closed-minded and give this game a try... at least buy it when it's on sale.
P.S.-Sorry for my broken english

Bought the Thief collection when it was on sale for $11. Never played the originals and wanted to play this first, to judge it without as much bias. After playing for two or so hours I thought it was alright and not as bad as people made it out to be.
Then, some things started to irritate me. Nitpicks I suppose, but after playing the original for a bit, the issues I had/have compounded. Contextual jumping is my biggest issue, having Garrett decide the best way to grab a ♥♥♥♥ing rope in front of him was to jump off the 3 story ledge he was on, straight into the ground below, killing him. This has happened more times than I can count in the 15 hours I've put in. The pseudo-AssCreed style 3rd Person climbing in certain places just feels like it shouldn't be there, and really is pointless. Every time I try to open a drawer in a desk, the contextual leaning decides I wanted to lean, not open the drawer.
Nearly every action you can do is contextual, causing issues as I've stated, and essentially turns everything into a small cutscene or an animation in which you've no control. Knocking out a guard, pickpocketing, even opening ♥♥♥♥ing drawers. It makes everything feel sluggish, even in the rare moments Garrett decides to skip the aftercare when knocking a guard out. What comes to mind is an attempt to mimic Deus Ex: Human Revolution's takedown system, and as much I love that game, that takedown system wasn't good there, or here.
The story, so far, is best to be ignored. Every supporting character seems to only be there to annoy you, Garrett seems to think he's discount Batman, being about as intelligent as the caped lunatic. I've gotten to the point where I've dropped the pretense of Garrett just being a thief, trying to stealth his way through the wallets and safes of poor saps, and just killing everyone in my path just to get through the game quicker.
The focus abilities seem to be damn pointless, the upgrade allowing you to see lock mechanisms when picking just makes it even more difficult to pick, as the pins actually fight against you now. The stealth Focus upgrade doesn't appear to do as advertised, that is, keeping you hidden in light for a brief moment. With the standard eye ability, the best thing you can do for yourself is drain the focus meter entirely, and just tap the focus button, as the ability will flash on and off, but highlightable objects will be highlighted for a moment. On the subject of safes, I have found maybe 2 combinations in the entire game, and at least one of them you get no matter what because of story reasons. I have found it to be more prudent to brute force or even flat out looking up the combination, as I'm not going to scour the entire city for some cobbler's damn safe combo, for 20 gold.
There are a lot of moments this game has where it could be fun, but it seems to be content with spoiling it as much as possible. On a more positive note, I absolutely love the swoop mechanic, and ignoring the focus ability for it, I enjoy the lockpicking as well.
The only reason I'm still playing is I can't stand not finishing a game, but as soon as I beat it, there is no way I'm touching it again. I suggest you don't bother with this.

Dishonored is a hundred times better than this shoddy ripoff.
The story is as generic as it can get, it definitely feels like a ripoff of Dishonored and it has a lamer villain than Turok Evolution's Cpt. Bruckner. Also their much touted "advanced mocap" is used with cutscenes where Garrett is just standing around with his mouth half-open, wich is the half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥explanation of Eidos for not using the superior acting skills (and sexier voice) of Stephen Russell.
Gameplay wise, it's your standard sleath fare, but with a game touting so many "choices" for tackling any given situation, you're VERY restricted on what you can or can't do, for instance, you can't jump and you can't use rope arrows on any wooden surface like in the old games, instead you can only use them on very specific places.
And be prepared to mash the X button, as there are plenty of QTEs that repeat over and over, one for opening windows and another one to move a large wooden plank. And that's not counting the same animations for opening safes, lockpicking doors or stealing paints.
And don't even bother attempting ghost runs, it doesn't have a "morality" system if you kill NPCs and it's not really worth the hassle to do ghost, you'll only have a miserable time if you do.
It has a rather serious bug with the sound engine, where you can hear NPCs right next to you, but they're at the other room or several feet away from you. One of the most important aspects for a game like this is completely botched.
Most of the missions are okay, with the highlight being the Bank Heist DLC mission, though it definitely losses some steam after a copy of the famous Craddle mission from Deadly Shadows.
Go play the first two games instead of this, the second game has a bigger and better bank heist mission, heck, go play Deadly Shadows if you're new to the series. Or better yet, get Dishonored instead of this.
It's rather ironic that Dishonored aimed at being up to the high quality standards of the old Thief games, but the new Thief 2014 ended up as the imitator. And a bad one at that.
Stay away, you'll feel robbed if you buy this.

I think the game is very very good, since I don't really play platform games, but I really love survival games set in apocalyptic scenarios. In my experience of platformers, the game is really good since the way they incorporate the survival aspect is quite good, quite realistic, e.g. if you kill an AI in the game, when your character comes home from a scavenge somewhere, then there will be realistic sounding conversations going on, and your character can become depressed, which requires meds to solve, or maybe a chill on a seat and maybe a smoke or something...
The only thing that really I think needs to change within a reasonable amount of time is a damn save system... "Run! Soldiers!" is the only thing I heard within 10 seconds of me being shot 3 times and then dying, indeed I slammed my mouse onto the table pad for cups cause I was annoyed sitting on my sofa **noob-rage here** - however, I would've liked to have been able to return to that spot, as for many people I feel the replay value is not high enough to encourage players to start playing again if one of their characters dies suddenly and muffs up their game story, technically yes obviously it is a part of the game, so players should technically play on regardless, but meh... You need to balance replay value, with the ease of returning to the previous place you was in the game...
I got this game for £3 in the steam sale, and I honesly feel it is quite a good game... I indeed did get other survival games, like Subnautica (I have NO affiliation what-so-ever, rather I'm just mentioning it), this has a save system, and so you can return to the point that you was, if you suddenly die in a, let's say, ironic way. However, then it would be too easy to return to where you was and death doesn't mean anything, however Subnautica is a FPS sandbox survival game, more so like Minecraft so technically I can't compare the two in exactly the same way...
I don't have exactly the most patience ever, but I've given TWOM a couple campaign attempts, using different players, and I feel the game does have replay value for what it cost me, as I really want to see what else happens in the game and be able to craft a multitude of weapons...
One thing to NOT forget, is the fact that DLC money is donated to CHARITY - YES DLC moneys (AFAIK) goes to Charities that actually help Children in war-zones, and this is no small thing. The world is in enough Kak as it is - and I like what the devs of TWOM have done.
Realistically I know that TWOM is probably not on sale any longer since the New Year celebrations are over, so maybe some people may not find as much replay value in the game and may see it less worth it when they have to pay full price, but I still do think the game will be worth it to someone who wants something new and is looking for some fun.
This game does NOT have multiplayer as it obviously indicates, however it took my friend a question to me to actually realise that the game doesn't include multiplayer (if she's reading this - you're amazing S!!!!). However, there are quite realistic situations in the game that I feel the devs really wanted to add to honestly reflect the FUBAR situations that survivors in war-zones are in.
There are some good easter-eggs per-se in the game, in the sense that they add a cool radio feature in the game that gives you updates on the current situation of the rebels in the game, some looters also let you live when you go to find food and items etc, which is a nice touch, because even though most survivors won't take the chance and would probably just shoot you in other games or real life to be fair, some survivors are happy to say "There's enough for all of us here!" - and I was quite happy with this, as he was rolling with his AKM...
I mean, yeah, the game is good, it's a platform game, you can't expect too much from a platform game unless you have good storyline elements, and some good nicely done features that really connect the atmosphere to you, it makes you involved in the game, as you don't want to be caught in peoples houses if they have guns or if they have knives even - however you get to make armour and, for firearms enthusiasts, like myself, you can even reload ammo. I mean you can't say load up some 77gr TMKs for your .223, or some x39 for your AK, however you can get gunpowder, you can get casings, and you can get "firearm parts", all which can be used in to reload ammo, and make the firearms themselves...
This is a nice feature, as in any situation that was like this, a reloading press technically would be a very very useful tool at the beginning of such a situation but anyway...
I don't want to give everything about the game away, but I do honestly think it was worth the investment. The characters have pretty good backstories, and you can see how the characters that you begin with are interconnected, in the sense that it describes the lives of the people and how they knew eachother, before the Civil war in the game began...
It seems to me that it tries to reflect the situation of Israel and Palestine, with the whole middle-eastern conflict in Syria, now I don't know this for sure what-so-ever, this is just my opinion, but the set-up of the game, minus the decals in English instead of Arabic etc, reflects something like this.
Good game...

This game really, really isnt for everyone. That being said though, I liked it quite a bit.Its quite short (took me less than an hour to complete) and its inner game gameplay consists of clicking something and waiting.  However, the outside go game gameplay (that sounds weird but stick with me) in exploring Nina's desktop and looking at her life through her own eyes is an incredibly immersive and rewarding experience. Even smaller details, such as hearing the sound of Nina's mouse clicking when you click the mouse immerses you as her. I also have to give major props to Nina for putting her body so out there, as I can imagine the backlash she might receive for it. Another thing i have to commend is the dialogue and general VO. Its not the best or most hollywood-esque sounding lines in a game, far from that in fact. As someone with a long distance girlfriend, it was incredible to see how naturally and closely it resembled my own relationship, at least at the begginnig. It feels like two akward people falling in love while playing a game, as opposed to two actors reading lines. In that sense its more a Silent Hill 2 style of voice acting, minus the creepiness, as opposed to an Until Dawn approach. So I do like this game, but I know fully its not for everyone. If you have the money to spare, then there is an interesting a unique autobiographical game here quite unlike most other things on the market.

I was very surprised how intimate and realistic 'Cibele' feels. Everything from the desktop folders to the selfies to the blog and chat logs read crude and awkward and what you expect a teen girl to feel. I was absolutely not that type of girl, so it was interesting to dive into the character and her life and get her know better. Get behind that wall of selfies and anime.
The only bummer is the end, though. It came up unexpected and without any explanation. Although that's what probably happened to that relationship in real life.
Fantastic work. Would love to play more games like this.

While it seems like an interesting concept, the game is frustrating as hell, mostly because of the policy. Seriously, are you guys so money starved that you go on and ask for premium currency for freaking flag patterns? I understand speed ups, I understand micro transactions like cool looking vanity items, but in a strategy game of one of the most well-known franchises, you go on and charge for the "amazing privilege" of making your coat of arms navy blue or stripped? Even the emblems are for sale only, save 3-4 of the most simplistic. And honestly even the artwork of the emblems seems sloppy and doesn't even have enough variety. Simply ridiculous and annoying.
Also, the game could not be more pay to win. And I know that there will be the crowd saying that "no you can very well create and gather all the items that you can buy with gold". While that might be true, it is only half true though. Because the amount of grinding and waiting required to achieve something someone who feels like emptying his pockets for Sega can achieve with a click, is comical. Crafting a single item/unit takes 2.5 days in the very best case and requires a ton of resources, especially early game. And while you struggle to get your barings, you go to a duel and have a same level player pound you with artillery and flaming arrows just because he appeased the coin hungry spirits of Sega with a couple of hard earned clicks.
And the final touch is the silly terraforming that is both frustrating and before getting the gang of it can just flood your entire map. Just one step closer to creating Total War: Farmville... battle the toughest vegetables and conquer your garden!
The game could be fun, some ideas are good. The implementation is really bad though, and the company policy, even worse.

Looking for a simple fun beat em up in the vein of Castle Crashers with a Viking theme? Then try Viking Squad. Supporting up to three players local and online you plunder loot for your Jarl (that you happened to curse by freeing Loki, good job) and ravage the lands to stop the chaos you started.
Mechanically you collect new gear and weapons through levels and plunder loot to buy and level up your stats. In combat you traverse levels moving up and down between four lanes and sliding to dodge enemy attacks at the last second. Each viking has their own speciality and play style with their own special attacks that you can charge which cost rune power. If things get overwhelming you can also unleash an ultimate attack to clear the room.
Viking Squad is a great game to introduce people to beat em up games  with colorful art direction, great cartoon viking theme, and a folk-rock soundtrack that makes replaying the game a good time. Short and sweet to beat once, but to do everything (achievements) will require multiple playthroughs.

Disclosure: I got it for free on steam but I play it mostly on PS4.
The game is fun, it's enjoyable for the art style and old-school beat'em up gameplay mechanics. You can customize weapons/armor to a point (they each have a stat boost or stat pull depending) so while you may like the way a particular armor looks, it may not be the most powerful or most wise choice to go into battle with.
I love the fact that it has co-op (up to 3 people total, so you and two friends) and you can also join into online games with other people, which was very helpful when I was trying to beat the game and needed some help on the harder levels.
Enemies get progressively harder as you go (or I'm just bad at games, your call) and really honing in on the dash and jumps can help get you out of trouble A LOT. Also being able to quickly bounce inbetween lanes is helpful to avoid enemy attacks while still being able to whittle down health on enemies and minimizing risk on your end if you don't have a lot of health or backup potions to get you through levels.
It's not a short game but not the longest game in the world, but provides you with a great experience overall across a variety of different level types. Plus there are some great boss battles that are super fun when playing with friends. Teamwork is a great way to defeat bosses, especially since you'll need all the help you can get on the later levels.
My recommendation is if you're looking for a great side-scrolling beat'em up you can play with your friends, plunder some treasure, and harness your inner viking, this is your game.

Sucks because the game was fun up until that point. I'm sure younger, more dedicated gamers with more time on their hands won't mind backtracking but we were not up for it. Not for Viking Squad at least.

The artwork was sweet to look at, the audio was nice to listen to and the stories were short enough that I could go through all of them in one sitting, and not have to keep coming back to the game. Even with only a basic knowledge of all the characters, it was still easy to know who they were and to even know what choices to choose to get the routes for certain characters.
This is one of the easiest games I have ever completed, in all honesty. It was very short, very simple fun, and it was a really lovely game to sit and play for a short while. I’d definitely recommend this to visual novels lovers who want a bit of a break from their usual games.

I really wish I liked this game more. I am a big supporter of games of all sorts of topics and ideas. The only problem is that I don't feel Cibele was well done.
Starting with what I enjoyed - its autobiographical and about subjects rarely tackled maturely in games. I also  enjoyed that Nina put pictures, poems, etc to ground the game as a game about her.
For what I didn't like - I really hate the whole "is it a game?" debate. But I really dislike it when I have no agency in games. This game is entirely driven by grinding in a bad fake-mmo and listening to voice-overs. You get emails you can "Respond" to, but there is absolutely no choice, exploration, or agency anywhere.
It should be mentioned that the fake mmo game is very poorly done. Pathfinding barely works, there are a few animations you have to watch over and over, Ichi and monsters can walk off the path. It just makes the game unenjoyable.
The story also ends abruptly. Maybe that is a thematic decision, but narratively it really seems to just shut the game down. Aside from one statement you do not really get any resolution or explanation to the events.
I also think Ichi's personality really rubs me the wrong way. He's really the kind of person I could not stand being around or listening to, so having to hear him talk for an hour was really grating. This is further compounded by the fact that the game crashed for me before the third cutscene was shown, so I had to listen through the mmo portion of the third act twice, which is easily the most annoying (for me).
I definitely think you should check it out if you want a game about mmos and sex and online relationships, but know that the narrative may end abruptly. Also understand that the "game" portion of the game is very taxing and unengaging.
